propositions: The gate matches field names globally as bare attribute names rather than resolving reads to their owning dataclass, allowing inert fields to pass when same-named attributes exist on unrelated configs.

The gate's false-negative class affects common field names like enabled, path, timeout, remote, branch, mode that are reused across multiple config dataclasses and therefore cannot be policed by the current global-name matcher.

A read must be resolved to the dataclass that declares the field by using section-attribute names, parameter annotations, local assignments, function return annotations, conditional branches, and cross-module call-site binding.

Four live fields newly flagged by the corrected gate (McpConfig.readonly, McpConfig.allow_llm, McpConfig.allow_jira_sync, JiraConfig.allow_insecure) require accurate read-via markers documenting their actual consumers rather than being triaged as inert.

Existing test files test_check_config_reads.py and test_check_config_reads_heldout.py must be migrated from the bare-name contract to the owner-resolution contract with updated fixtures and inverted assertions.
Any existing read-via marker pointing to a closed rebar ticket must be surfaced by a reporting function so expired exemptions do not persist silently.
